data.title: Nearly nine months on, BIRAC yet to name startups under RDI fund
data.description:
It has been nearly nine months since the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a second-level fund manager, opened its first call for proposals for biotechnology (bi­otech) startups under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) fund. Yet, no formal announcement on the selected startups has been made. 
While the Technology Development Board (TDB), another second-level fund manager, has announced its first cohort of companies and is preparing to select the second, BIRAC has yet to make a formal announcement, despite having shortlisted seven to eight companies. 
A detailed email sent to the Department of Science and Technology and BIRAC seeking an update on the selection process, reasons for the delay and expected disbursement timelines did not elicit a response. 
One of the sticking points has been the funding structure, said some founders. Unlike TDB, which is extending low-interest loans, BIRAC has proposed a combination of debt and equity financing. According to several founders, negotiations have dragged on over the investment terms and the extent of equity dilution that startups may have to accept. 
At the launch of the call for proposals in February this year, BIRAC had said the evaluation of applications would be completed within eight weeks of receiving proposals, with funds expected to be disbursed within 12 weeks of evaluation. However, the process has dragged on well beyond the stipulated timelines. 
A person at BIRAC involved in the selection process said, “The funding structure is an important consideration. While low-interest loans offer a relati­vely straightforward financing route, a combination of debt and equity requires clarity on valuation, dilution, and other terms. That is why negotiations are taking longer than anticipated.” 
BIRAC’s relative inexperien­ce in structuring debt and equity investments is also understood to have contributed to the delay. Traditionally, the organisation has operated largely as a grant-giving institution. Working out investment term sheets and agreements under the RDI framework is taking additional time, sources said. 
However, several sources familiar with the process said the applications were in the final stage, with the finer details of the agreements being ironed out. The formal announcement is likely to follow once the agreements are finalised. 
The delay, meanwhile, has been weighing on startups awaiting funding, particularly those working on capital-intensive biotech projects. One founder, whose startup is part of the maiden cohort, said rising costs of manpower, equipment, and raw materials had pushed up project expenses. 
“Compared with the beginning of the year, when we submitted our applications and detailed our project plans, expenses have risen by around 10 per cent. The uncertainty over the timing of funding has complicated financial planning,” the founder said. “By the time the funding comes through, the original project cost estimates may no longer hold.” 
Another founder raised concerns over the uncertainty surrounding limited partner commitments, which were based on earlier business valuations and revenue projections. 
“The commitments were made based on certain valuations and revenue projections. With the funding process getting delayed, those assumptions are changing. It creates uncertainty for both the startup and the investors who are expected to participate,” the founder said. 
The RDI framework provides financing of up to 50 per cent of the assessed project cost, with startups required to arrange the remaining amount through self-financing or commercial sources. 
Consequently, a few startups have written separately to BIRAC, flagging concerns over the delay and seeking clarity on disbursement timelines. Some founders said they received tim­ely responses, while others poin­ted to delays in communication.
“There has been very little communication on the status of applications. We (startups) have invested considerable time and resources in preparing proposals, but there is no clear mechanism to track the status of applications or when a decision can be expected. We do not even know the complete list of companies selected for the first cohort,” one of the founders quoted above added. 
While several government schemes provide adequate data on their respective websites to showcase progress, the RDI fund does not have a publicly accessible dashboard tracking applications received, shortlisted, approved, and funded.

data.title: Airtel overtakes HDFC Bank to become India's most valuable brand: Report
data.description:
Airtel has been ranked as India’s most valuable brand by Kantar, a marketing data and analytics firm, in 2026 displacing HDFC Bank from the number one spot.
 
“This is the first time a telecom provider has claimed the No.1 position in the Kantar BrandZ Top 100 Most Valuable Indian Brands ranking since its launch in 2014. The telecom giant has grown 5 per cent in the last year to reach a brand value of $43.2 billion,” Kantar said in its release on the brand rankings. 
 
“Airtel is a brilliant example of a brand with strong brand equity and a global footprint. It is one of the few Indian brands to have achieved a global presence. It is also part of the global top 100,” Soumya Mohanty, managing director, South Asia, Kantar, told Business Standard.
 
 
In its methodology, Kantar takes into account the financial value, the brand contribution and the brand value.
 
“Worth a combined $460.3 billion, India’s Kantar BrandZ Top 100 Most Valuable Brands remain a powerful engine of economic growth, with their total value equivalent to 11 per cent of the country’s GDP. Overall, the value of the ranking has declined 12 per cent year-on-year, as brands manage the pressures of moving towards AI-enabled transformation,” the report.
 
The report also added that financial services remains the largest category by value, and represents 29 per cent of the Indian Top 100’s total. Five of this year’s top 10 risers come from the financial services sector, indicating its continued resilience.

data.title: Keystone Realtors to launch ₹5K cr worth housing properties in MMR by March
data.description:
Realty firm Keystone Realtors Ltd will launch housing properties worth Rs 5,000 crore for sale by March next year in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) as it remains bullish on consumer demand, a top company official said.

Mumbai-based Keystone Realtors, which is one of the leading real estate developers in the country, sells properties under the 'Rustomjee' brand.

In an interview with PTI, the company's Chairman and Managing Director Boman Irani exuded confidence that it would easily achieve the sales bookings or pre-sales target of Rs 5,000 crore for the 2026-17 fiscal.

"In the first half of this fiscal, our sales bookings stood at around Rs 2,000 crore, which is 40 per cent of our total guidance for the entire 2026-27. In the real estate sector, sales are generally higher in the second half because of festive demand. So, we are on track to meet the target," he said.

 

During the first six months of this fiscal, the company's sales bookings grew 11 per cent to Rs 2,041 crore from Rs 1,839 crore in the year-ago period.

In the entire 2025-26 fiscal year, the company's sales bookings stood at Rs 4,022 crore.

Asked about launches, Irani said the company launches projects worth Rs 2,000 crore in the first half of this fiscal year and another Rs 1,000 crore worth of properties in October.

He said the launch pipeline remains strong and the company would launch Rs 5,000 crore worth of residential properties by March.

The company has kept a target to launch Rs 8,000 crore worth properties for sale during the entire 2026-27 fiscal.

"Redevelopment in Mumbai continues to remain a core strategic focus, offering immense potential for sustained value creation. As one of the most preferred redevelopment players in the MMR region, we are uniquely positioned to capture these opportunities and strengthen our leadership in this segment," Irani said.

Incorporated in 1995, Keystone Realtors has completed 41 projects so far. It has 19 ongoing projects and 19 forthcoming projects. So far, the company has delivered over 30 million square feet of construction area, with a pipeline of over 45 million square feet of construction area in the works.

data.title: Arizona investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents
data.description:
By David Thomas The state of Arizona ??has opened a criminal investigation into  OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," ??Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday. 
A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona ‌state law was being violated  on an ongoing basis. 
"The  state of Arizona is very worried about this, and we  are looking at it from multiple angles," Mayes told a press conference in Chicago. 
Mayes declined to identify the other companies her office was investigating. She said her office had been in contact with Arizona banks,  but declined to name them or give their responses. 
 
A spokesperson for ‌OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 
The banking  industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Reuters reported last month that ‌major US banks have  been blocking third-party AI agents from ‌operating inside customer accounts and making transactions. 
Mayes' comments come two ‌days ??after California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI for allegedly developing  a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had carried out cyberattacks independently. 
OpenAI  did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on that lawsuit, but the company has acknowledged ‌a general need for more transparency around rogue AI behavior and said ‌it was reinforcing its safeguards. On September 16, the company published a new framework for disclosing such incidents, saying it would err on the side of transparency "even when significance is uncertain."

data.title: House Democrats move to probe Trump family, top administration officials
data.description:
The top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee is laying the groundwork for long-promised investigations into the Trump administration, which are set to begin with the new Congress in January.
 
Representative Robert Garcia of California, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee when Democrats take control, sent letters directing members of President Donald Trump’s family and top administration officials to preserve documents. The move is an early step towards launching investigations into the president and his administration.
 
The letters, released on Wednesday, cover a wide range of potential investigations, including alleged financial conflicts involving Trump’s family, misconduct at the Department of Homeland Security and the administration’s handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein.
 
 
“Oversight Democrats are fighting to put an end to this Administration’s self-dealing, misconduct, and abuse,” Garcia said in a statement. “These investigations will lay the groundwork for legislation which helps all Americans. This is just the beginning.”
 
Those targeted by the letters include two of Trump’s sons, Vice President JD Vance, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law.
 
The letters offer an early glimpse of how Democrats plan to use their newly won congressional majority to scrutinise Trump and his administration. As favourable election results rolled in for Democrats on the night of the midterms, Garcia posted a warning on social media: “Lawyer up.”

data.title: Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden
data.description:
Rising fuel costs are complicating Walmart's efforts to keep prices low even as strong growth in its delivery and membership businesses prompted the retailer to raise annual forecasts ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season.

The world's largest retailer, seen as a bellwether for US consumer health, reported a 5.2% rise in third-quarter revenue to $188.84 billion, beating expectations.

It now expects fiscal 2027 net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2%, up from its previous forecast of 4% to 5%, but still below analysts' expectations for growth of 5.5%, according to data compiled by LSEG.

CEO John Furner said surging diesel and transportation costs had added about $2 billion in incremental expenses this year and could hamper efforts to keep prices low as consumers head into the holiday shopping season.

 

"We will do everything we can in terms of efficiency," Furner said on a post-earnings call, adding that pricing "really depends on transportation costs and input costs as we move forward."

HOLIDAY PLANS

Walmart has cut prices on thousands of grocery and general merchandise items this year as Americans seek cheaper options amid high inflation and an Iran War that has pushed up fuel prices. Consumer sentiment, while improving in November, remains weak.

Rising freight and logistics costs have squeezed profits across the retail and consumer goods industries, though Walmart has partly offset the impact through nearly $3 billion in tariff refunds, Furner said.

Still, executives struck an upbeat tone about the holiday shopping season.

"It's game time," Furner said, noting that Walmart had sold 1 million more Thanksgiving turkeys than a year earlier after cutting the price of its holiday meal basket to its lowest since the programme was launched in 2022.

The retailer has leaned on its stores as "digital fulfilment nodes" for e-commerce orders and its higher-margin third-party marketplace, which posted gains during the quarter.

That has helped support sales as growth in store visits has slowed from a year earlier.

"The margin story is outrunning the traffic story right now," said David Wagner, head of equity at Aptus Capital Advisors.

The retailer has pushed deeper into membership, e-commerce and marketplace businesses to diversify revenue and support margins. Last month, it launched a bundled membership offer for its Walmart+ loyalty programme and its Sam's Club wholesale unit. Membership fee revenue rose by double digits in the three months through October.

Its push into faster delivery has also helped drive repeat purchases, while customers using the service were more likely to sign up for its membership programme, the company said.

Overall, US e-commerce sales increased 23%, compared with 28% growth a year earlier.

Walmart raised its annual adjusted earnings forecast to $2.84 to $2.89 per share from $2.80 to $2.87 previously. Analysts expect $2.88 per share.

Adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share edged past estimates, while operating expenses rose 5% to $40.01 billion.

Walmart shares fell about 2%. The stock has gained about 14% this year and is on track for a fourth straight annual gain.

data.title: Tata Trusts board meet on November 20; Tata Sons listing not on agenda
data.description:
A board meeting of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), a key entity of Tata Trusts and a core shareholder of Tata Sons, is scheduled for November 20.
 
It is being seen as a build up to the Tata Sons board meeting of November 26, when the critical issue of the holding company’s stock exchange listing is expected to come up.
 
However, according to sources, the proposed listing of Tata Sons is not on the agenda of the SDTT meeting. It is learnt that approval of grants would be discussed at Friday’s meeting of the trustees, including Chairman Noel Tata, Vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh and two others — Bhaskar Bhat and Neville Tata (Noel Tata’s son). Among other things, a grant to Jehangir Hospital, chaired by Jehangir HC Jehangir, is learnt to be on the agenda. Jehangir is a trustee at Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) —another core shareholder of Tata Sons. Tata Trusts, of which SDTT and SRTT are key entities, is the largest shareholder of Tata Sons with a 66 per cent stake.

data.title: GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait
data.description:
After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolled out across the globe on Thursday, gaining rapturous early reviews for the most anticipated video game release in history.

The game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, raced to the top of Metacritic's all-time gaming leaderboard with a score of 99, a mark matched by only one other title, Nintendo's 1998 classic "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".

The rollout began as the clock struck midnight in New Zealand and moved across time zones from Tokyo to Miami, prompting launch parties, posts from world leaders and even some companies giving staff the day off to play.

 

"It is the best game that's ever been made and we're only 20 minutes deep," said 33-year-old Asif Mir as he started to play and livestream just after midnight in Sydney.

In London, gamers counted down to the release at parties across the city.

"Today has been a day that I have waited for my whole life," said 20-year-old influencer Archie Whitby. "To be living it, it feels almost dystopian. It doesn't feel real."

Miami, the inspiration for the game's fictional Vice City setting, was one of the last places to get in on the action.

The city's NBA team, the Miami Heat, celebrated with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks, with the court and stadium adorned with the game's colours of neon pink and blue.

Mia Pazan travelled to Miami for the launch.

"I came here, number one, because I love GTA VI. I played literally all the games," she said, adding that as a Latina woman she loved the fact that there was a protagonist — co-lead character Lucia Caminos — reflecting her identity.

"I really identify with Lucia a lot," she added.

Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles, with many taking time off work — or calling in sick — to play the latest instalment in a franchise that since its 1997 debut has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

"It's the Star Wars of this generation," said Joost van Dreunen, adjunct professor at NYU Stern School of Business.

"It's a synchronized, shared event. So millions of people will all want to be there the first couple of days, the first few weeks of experiencing it as it goes live."

Strong initial reviews of the game — available on Sony's PlayStation 5 and Microsoft's Xbox Series X and S consoles — helped push Take-Two Interactive's US shares higher on Wednesday.

GREAT STRESS RELIEF' FOR FEMALE GAMERS

The original "Grand Theft Auto" looks basic by today's standards, with a storyline — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — that angered politicians and parents, even as it delighted fans.

But as the series progressed it became increasingly sophisticated, mixing its trademark crime, driving and morally dubious missions with activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture.

"Grand Theft Auto V", released in 2013, was set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles. The action now moves to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game's take on Florida.

Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved — just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

GTA VI could prove less provocative than its predecessors, said Tore Olsson, a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

"There's no doubt that Jason and Lucia of VI will be criminals, and they'll be regularly breaking the law," said Olsson.

"But I don't think the new game will require players to enact wanton slaughter, and it may indeed penalize those who choose to play that way."

Having Lucia as a lead character should help address complaints about a lack of playable female characters in previous iterations of GTA. Women will be an estimated four out of 10 GTA VI players in the US, according to a Bain survey.

"Since you can do all that brutal stuff like running people over or hitting them, my first thought was that it's mostly for male players," said 30-year-old Tokyo worker Suzana Onoda.

"After trying it out, well, I think getting to beat people up is a great stress relief for women as well."

STRONG REVIEWS: 'TRULY ASTONISHING', 'A MASTERPIECE'

Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that more than 17 million copies had been sold so far for over $1.65 billion.

With the main part of the game estimated to take around 50 hours to complete, full reactions were not available immediately. But initial reviews from gaming industry experts were almost universal in their high praise.

Entertainment website GamesRadar+ said Rockstar had built a world of "truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality". The release "will be talked about for years to come" and was "well worth the 13-year wait", said PC Games. Various outlets called it a "masterpiece".

While some economists have warned about lost productivity as gamers take time off from work, consumer analysts said the economy could also receive a boost from sales of the game, consoles, storage upgrades and even food delivery services.

In India, home to hundreds of millions of gamers, Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted Grand Theft Auto-inspired social media content and some firms gave employees the day off.

On Australia's southern island of Tasmania, family-run fragrance shop Whiff-it! will close for a week after 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown persuaded his mother to give him and his brother time off to play.

"She was really against it at first," said Bowen-Brown. "I had to say, mum, please, please, I need it... I've been waiting 13 years to play the game."

data.title: Anthropic raises $81 bn, set to secure $1.8 trn valuation in Nasdaq debut
data.description:
Anthropic was on course to secure a $1.8 trillion valuation when its shares start trading on Thursday, in a historic debut that pits promises of artificial intelligence (AI) as an economic game-changer against fears of a market bubble and risks to humanity.
 
The stock was set to open at $99.82, about 20 per cent higher than the initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, according to indications as of 8:20 pm IST on Thursday.
 
The Claude chatbot maker’s upsized IPO, together with Tuesday’s earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week. The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to a sector where euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks.
 
 
AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-centre-sceptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections. Investors who once embraced the boom have turned sceptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the mounting debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.
 
Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record after increasing the size of its offering, in a deal that values the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion and defied concerns over AI and tech fundraising.
 
In a sign of strong investor demand, Anthropic priced its shares at $83 each, above its initial range of $70 to $78.
 
Reuters was first to report on Wednesday that Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to float, had increased the number of shares it was selling by about 19 per cent to 980 million.
 
Anthropic’s IPO eclipses the debut of Elon Musk’s SpaceX in June. Its total deal size is $107.3 billion, including another $26 billion that Anthropic is raising through a private placement of shares, the filings showed.
 
Nasdaq futures rose nearly 2 per cent on Thursday, bolstering expectations for a strong Anthropic debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks.
 
Chipmakers and cloud companies, which have raised hundreds of billions of dollars to fund their massive spending plans, have in recent weeks come under pressure due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs and the sudden exit of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang.
 
Anthropic has, meanwhile, faced questions about its outlook and ability to sustain rapid growth as competition intensifies.
 
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are lead underwriters for Anthropic’s IPO, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate.
 
Anthropic’s annualised revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing.
 
Underscoring its growing business foothold, Anthropic said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year. But to sustain that growth, Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026.
 
Anthropic also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity. Revenue rose to $16.96 billion in the third quarter, up 47 per cent from the second.
 
The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter. The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating items related to bonds convertible into its shares.
 
Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Alphabet’s Google, to train and operate AI models.

data.title: MCA seeks to broaden scope of CSR spending; to include PM internship scheme
data.description:
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) has proposed legislative amendments to expand the list of activities on which companies can spend their corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds and to make the activities’ impact assessment voluntary.
 
As per the proposal, promoting employment, enhancing vocational skills for the youth and their participation in the Prime Minister Internship Scheme are eligible to be covered under business’ CSR projects.
 
This inclusion could see companies channelise a portion of their CSR funds for candidates joining them under the PM Internship Scheme.
 
The changes require amendments to both schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014, showed the draft orders released by the ministry for public feedback. The proposals seek to facilitate businesses to be even more socially, economically, and environmentally responsible, the ministry said in a public notice.
 
Companies Act mandates businesses with a net worth of at least Rs 500 crore, turnover of Rs 1,000 crore or net profit of Rs 5 crore in the immediately preceding financial year to spend at least 2 per cent of their average net profits over the three immediately preceding financial years on eligible CSR activities.
 
Non-profit (Section 8) companies, foreign companies with a branch or project office in India, and holding or subsidiary companies are also covered under the CSR provisions, if they independently meet one of the thresholds.
 
“In 2025, one in four Indians aged 15 to 29 was neither working nor in education or training, so it is welcome that the draft CSR rules explicitly recognise career counselling and participation in the Prime Minister Internship Scheme,” said Priya Naik, Founder and CEO, Samhita and Collective Good Foundation, citing Periodic Labour Force Survey annual report 2025.
 
The proposed revised Schedule VII broadens the existing categories of eligible activities by including mental health, telemedicine, and prevention and treatment of substance abuse under healthcare. Welfare measures for transgender persons, children, youth and persons with disabilities have also been proposed as eligible activities.
 
On the other hand, the draft excludes one-off events, financing of government schemes and contributions to the corpus funds of any entity from eligible activities under CSR. Notably, contributions in kind involving a company's own products or services would also not qualify, except when given for immediate relief distribution during disaster management.
 
“Distributing one’s own products free of cost has often worked more as brand promotion than as social responsibility. The exclusions draw a clear line between genuine impact and freebies, events or idle corpus funds,” said Amit Agarwal, Senior Partner, Nangia & Co LLP.
 
While the existing Schedule VII expressly mentions livelihood enhancement projects, the proposed draft does not. It, however, retains vocational skills, welfare of economically backward groups, or rural development.
 
Naik called for explicit support for livelihood enhancement that helps small businesses, especially those led by women, reach new customers, access affordable finance and create local jobs.
 
The ministry also proposed to make impact assessment of CSR projects voluntary for companies, irrespective of their CSR spending obligations. Presently, assessment is mandatory for companies with an average CSR obligation of Rs 10 crore or more, for projects of Rs 1 crore or more.
 
Further, international organisations, which at present can only be engaged for design, monitoring, evaluation and capacity building, would be able to act as implementing agencies if they have their global headquarters in India, once the proposals are implemented.
 
Other proposed inclusions are climate change, natural farming, rainwater harvesting, clean energy and e-waste management under environmental sustainability, along with contributions to the National Sports Development Fund, medical care for sportspersons, sports infrastructure and coach development programmes.
 
The ministry also proposed allowing implementing agencies to voluntarily surrender their registration numbers, if they have fully utilised their CSR funds and met other conditions.
 
The government also intends to cancel or deactivate registrations on grounds of fraud, misrepresentation, misuse of CSR funds and failure to meet eligibility conditions.
 
Agencies facing cancellation would be given at least 30 days to reply to a notice. Those whose registrations are cancelled would be barred from applying afresh for three years, unless the cancellation order provides otherwise.
